summary: The ohlcv canonical-table migration is feasible but must be split into explicit, validated phases. The biggest risk is redirecting L3 readers before the canonical table is validated and a compatibility view exists. Reader redirection and live-trading timing require Claude/human oversight.
consensus_findings: The migration needs a compatibility view to keep old readers working during cutover.
Reader redirection must happen after canonical-table validation and writer cutover.
ML feature references need to be enumerated before the compatibility view is removed.
blind_spots: Downstream aggregation jobs outside the current repo.
Real-time consumers that cache ohlcv aggregates.
major_risks: L3 reader redirection before canonical table validation (RISK-002).
Reader redirection too ambiguous for Codex alone (RISK-007).
task_graph_constraints: T-001 Create canonical ohlcv table must complete before backfill.
T-002 Backfill canonical table must be idempotent and verified with row-count parity.
T-003 Compatibility view must exist before any reader redirection task.
T-004 Writer cutover to canonical table must complete before reader redirection.
T-005 Redirect L3 readers must depend on validation of canonical table and compatibility view.
T-005 must be implementation_agent claude or human.
T-006 Integration verification must run after all other tasks.
required_integration_tasks: Row-count parity between old table, canonical table, and compatibility view.
Regime feature output parity before/after redirection.
required_verification_gates: Schema diff test and SELECT parity test.
Feature pipeline dry-run against new schema.
IAM role definition test for backfill job.
route_to_claude: Reader redirection orchestration and cross-file reader impact analysis (T-005).
route_to_human: Live-trading timing decision for reader redirection.
must_not_dispatch_to_codex: Reader redirection orchestration without human/Claude review.
